selection.rationale: The measured unit is one complete batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward; the independently measured baseline is latency_ms=4.237417 (project.json original_baseline; current revision f2cfe831 has no accepted bundles installed). execution_timeline-1221e205 shows 88 kernels with kernel_active_union_us=4066.6 vs gaps_between_kernels_us=81.1 over a 4147.7us span on a single serial stream (compute_overlap_us=0.0): the invocation is GPU-compute-bound, so only removing GPU kernel time moves latency_ms materially (host/launch-side ceiling ~2%). Leaf-family diagnostics: aten::conv2d 3043.1us (20 calls), aten::batch_norm 428.5us (20 calls), aten::relu 341.9us (17), max_pool2d 200.1us, add_ 121.0us. All 20 batch_norm kernels sit directly after a bias-free conv2d (observed conv2d signatures have bias=None) inside a ResNetConvLayer (17 calls: embedder stem + 16 stage convs) or ResNetShortCut (3 calls) running with training=False and frozen running stats (observed batch_norm signatures), so every site admits the exact inference fold scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W'=W*scale, b'=beta-scale*mean. Selecting all 20 module calls as one joint bundle keeps the strategy coherent (partial folding would mix eager BN with folded sites) and every edit is a direct module callable boundary under the legacy binding backend that explicitly replaces the conv+BN bundle, so no inherited required call inside those bundles is left dangling; the unchanged aten::relu/max_pool2d/add_ work continues to execute in the surviving parents. Lazy one-time folding at first invocation is legitimate setup per the binding contract and lands in quality/warmup (warmup=2 precede repeats=5), outside timed repeats. Precision policy is untouched (FP32 fold arithmetic only; TF32 off, no autocast/quantization, cudnn.benchmark unchanged); cost is one folded parameter copy ~45MB, which peak_allocated_bytes reports but no constraint binds to latency_ms for this request.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing forward of all 17 ResNetConvLayer calls (groups 836e80426d566f8f5dce, 0022893ec8c1ceea869f, 39b672d8d4bea8959c44, 867f8d20e37fedce71c4, c30ffc96e594cd4d7734) and all 3 ResNetShortCut calls (groups 04fe5ffd91a3ecdc1ced, 9c1e6f2c47a84d7de11d, 4e7e7ecf95e285fe008e) with a lazily-cached BN-folded F.conv2d(x, W', b') followed by the unchanged activation eliminates all 20 aten::batch_norm kernels, i.e. 428.5us of serial GPU leaf time (10.5% of the 4066.6us busy union), while conv kernels keep their time up to a negligible bias epilogue; expected latency_ms drops from ~4.24 to ~3.8 (-8..11%) and images_per_second (exact reciprocal at fixed batch) rises proportionally, keeping the 0.95 memory-goal throughput ratio. Numerical fidelity was pre-validated on the worker CPU python (transformers 5.16.1, torch 2.13.0) with the exact frozen weights and exact batch=32 workload input: folding all 20 sites reproduces the full 1000-class logits with max_abs_err=7.6e-6, 0/32000 violations of atol+rtol*|ref| (atol=rtol=1e-4), exact top-1 preserved (min reference top1-top2 margin 0.1446, four orders of magnitude above the observed error), and the warm cached path is bit-stable across repeated invocations. This remains a hypothesis until the framework's independent GPU validation confirms the quality checks and the wall-latency reduction; if GPU conv timing shifts under folded weights or the bias epilogue costs more than expected, realized benefit will be smaller than the removed BN leaf time, and follow-up elementwise opportunities (exact relu-maxpool fusion in the stem, add-relu fusion in ResNetBasicLayer) remain available as separate candidates.

proposal.rationale: Objective: minimize latency_ms of one complete offline batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode()). Baseline latency_ms=4.237417 (project.json original_baseline; revision f2cfe831 has no installed bundles, so requires/replaces are empty). Evidence: execution_timeline-1221e205 shows 88 kernels with kernel_active_union_us=4066.6 vs gaps_between_kernels_us=81.1 on one serial stream (compute_overlap_us=0.0), i.e. GPU-compute-bound, so only removing serial GPU kernel time moves latency; leaf diagnostics attribute 3043.1us to aten::conv2d (20), 428.5us to aten::batch_norm (20), 341.9us to aten::relu (17), 200.1us to max_pool2d, 121.0us to add_. Strategy: all 20 selected conv sites (17 ResNetConvLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut module calls) run with training=False and a frozen eval-mode BatchNorm2d directly after a bias-free conv (observed conv2d signatures have bias=None), so each conv+BN pair collapses exactly into one F.conv2d(x, W', b') with scale=gamma/sqrt(running_var+eps), W'=W*scale, b'=beta-scale*running_mean, followed by the site's unchanged activation module call (ReLU/Identity; shortcuts have none). This removes all 20 aten::batch_norm kernels (428.5us of serial leaf time, ~10.5% of the busy union) while every aten::conv2d kernel still executes (now with a negligible per-channel bias epilogue), and all aten::relu/max_pool2d/add_ work continues in surviving parents. Selecting all 20 module calls as one joint bundle keeps the policy coherent (partial folding would mix eager BN with folded sites); each edit is a direct module callable boundary under the legacy binding backend, so no functional dispatch overhead is added on unrelated operators. Fidelity: pure FP32 fold arithmetic; TF32 stays disabled, no autocast/quantization/cudnn.benchmark change; the transform is algebraically exact for eval-mode BN up to FP32 rounding. The selection records CPU pre-validation with the exact frozen weights and the exact batch=32 workload input: max_abs_err=7.6e-6 over the full 1000-class logits vs the atol=rtol=1e-4 budget (0/32000 violations), exact top-1 preserved (min top1-top2 margin 0.1446, four orders above the error), warm cached path bit-stable across repeated invocations; this remains a hypothesis until the framework's independent GPU validation confirms quality and wall latency. No previous-feedback.txt or previous-candidate exists at this revision (first attempt). Runtime policy: the replacement takes the folded path only for the observed signature class (single 4-D float32 CUDA tensor on the folded weights' device with matching in_channels, modules in eval, grad disabled, no extra args) and otherwise re-enters the untouched parent forward, so unsupported signatures, a flipped training flag or an unexpected grad-enabled caller cannot corrupt outputs; route labels are self-reported via context['record_route'] ('bn_folded_conv2d', 'fallback:signature', 'fallback:fold_setup_failed') as diagnostics only. Every invocation executes the real conv kernels on the current inputs: no output caching, no fixture precomputation, no CUDA Graph capture (Python replacement invocations remain observable for coverage). Eliminated calls: the 40 inner module boundaries (20 ...convolution Conv2d + 20 ...normalization BatchNorm2d calls) and the 20 aten.batch_norm.default functional calls under them. Their consumers remain valid because each replacement returns a tensor with the same shape, dtype, device and (up to fold rounding) values as the parent conv->BN output: downstream max_pool2d, stage/residual add_ and subsequent layers consume unchanged tensors; aten::conv2d kernels still run inside the replacements via F.conv2d; aten::relu still runs through the unchanged activation modules; the profiler record_function annotations that instrumented the removed conv/bn module boundaries are observation instrumentation and disappear with those boundaries during profiled recapture, which does not affect outputs. Expected effect: latency_ms ~4.24 -> ~3.8 (-8..-11%); images_per_second is the exact reciprocal at fixed batch and rises proportionally, keeping the offline row's 0.95 memory-goal throughput ratio satisfied.

setup_work.when: build(context) (installation; before quality tracking and before the adapter's invocation starts). No per-invocation setup: folded tensors are computed once and reused; adapter.reset() only calls model.eval(), and eval-mode parameters of this inference-only warm-model lifecycle are invariant across invocations.
actions: For each of the 20 selected module sites: read conv.weight (bias is None at every site), bn.weight/bias/running_mean/running_var/eps, and compute scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W'=W*scale (per out-channel), b'=beta-scale*running_mean under torch.no_grad() on the model's CUDA device, then .contiguous(). Roughly 20 small elementwise setup kernels plus 20 tiny reductions, executed once at install.

Capture (W', b'), stride/padding/dilation/groups and the activation module reference in per-site closures; no model parameter, buffer or module attribute is mutated (the parent forward and its parameters stay intact for guarded fallback); no module.forward wrapper is installed by the candidate; no CUDA Graphs are captured.
setup_work.retained_memory: Folded weight copies total 11,171,008 float32 elements (~44.7 MB) plus 20 folded bias vectors (2,752 floats, ~11 KB), retained in closures for the candidate lifetime on the CUDA device alongside the untouched originals (~44.7 MB). framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes therefore rise by roughly the folded-copy size (setup/installation allocation, reported here, not hidden); framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per run but still reflects these steady-state live allocations during the forward, so the offline row's peak_allocated_bytes memory goal may report a slightly higher peak (activation buffers dominate the run peak). This counter increase is the accounting cost of retaining a folded copy, not a physical-memory saving claim; the request's latency_ms objective carries no memory constraint (the 0.95 images_per_second ratio belongs to the offline row's memory goal, and throughput improves with latency).

quality_risks: Fold rounding vs assert_close(atol=rtol=1e-4) and require_exact_top1: reported CPU pre-validation shows max_abs_err=7.6e-6 with a 0.1446 minimum top1-top2 margin, but cuDNN may pick a different conv algorithm for bias-bearing folded weights on GPU, shifting the error; only the framework's independent GPU validation of the full logits and exact top-1 against the reference confirms fidelity.

Negative control (reference+1 corruption must stay rejected) operates on reference logits in the harness; both reference and actual forwards use the same replaced path with identical, bit-stable folded parameters, so the check remains well defined and passing, but it is re-verified rather than assumed.

Realized latency gain may be smaller than the removed 428.5us of aten::batch_norm leaf time if folded conv kernels (bias epilogue, possibly different cuDNN algorithm choice with cudnn.benchmark=False heuristics) run slower than the bias-free originals.

peak_allocated_bytes for the offline memory goal rises by roughly the ~44.7 MB retained folded copies (steady-state live allocation visible per run); no latency constraint is attached, and the 0.95 throughput ratio is unaffected, but the memory goal value itself will not improve.

Any replacement that hits its guard (unexpected signature/state, grad enabled, training flag) falls back to the unmodified parent for that call, which stays numerically correct but forfeits that site's speedup; fallback occurrences are visible through record_route labels and runtime coverage.

Deterministic setup policies from common.configure(): torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), torch.manual_seed(20261020).

The workload input is exactly pixels = images[torch.arange(batch, device=device) % images.shape[0]].contiguous(), where images is the (3,3,224,224) float32 NCHW tensor loaded from assets pixels.npy; batch comes from request['workload']['batch'] (32 for this frozen request), never an embedded constant.

The measured invocation is a single complete forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits executed under @torch.inference_mode(), with the model in eval() mode; no training, gradients, optimizer, sampling or communication exists in the workload.

Quality fidelity checks that bound any optimization: full logits must satisfy assert_close against the reference with atol=rtol=1e-4, and integer top-1 labels must match exactly (torch.equal on argmax(-1) over all 1000 classes, require_exact_top1); the +1 corruption negative control must remain rejected. No accuracy or convergence claim beyond this reference fidelity.

latency_ms is the per-batch-call wall latency of that one forward at fixed batch=32, and images_per_second = batch*1e9/elapsed_ns is its exact reciprocal; no performance constraint is attached to latency_ms for this request (the workloads.json images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 constraint belongs to the offline row's peak_allocated_bytes memory goal).

The adapter must use context['device'] (the worker-bound CUDA device) for the model, input tensors and device placement instead of choosing a physical GPU, and must not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time.

Statistics queries (max_memory_allocated) stay in metrics() outside the timer; run() must not duplicate the framework's synchronize/peak-reset boundary operations because the source has no internal completion point.

The online (batch=1) workload row and the held-out unseen_batch (batch=7) workload in workloads.json are not part of this frozen request; other workload variants would supply a different batch through the same adapter.
